answer.answer: The Scheme for Prevention of Alcoholism and Substance Abuse is a government initiative that provides financial assistance to support NGOs in addressing addiction comprehensively [E02]. The scheme, initiated in 1987 and revised as of October 1, 2008, aims to support prevention of addiction and rehabilitation of drug users with a rights-based approach [E03]. Its objectives include creating awareness about the ill-effects of substance abuse to individuals, families, workplaces and society [E03], alleviating consequences of drug and alcohol dependence [E03], and evolving community-based services for identification, motivation, detoxification, counselling, after care and rehabilitation of drug users [E03]. The scheme also facilitates research, training, documentation and collection of relevant information [E03]. Key strategies include developing culture-specific prevention and treatment models, promoting community participation, creating trained human resource personnel, facilitating networking among stakeholders, and promoting continuous monitoring and evaluation [E03].
